I margini spiculati («corona radiata»),:
Spiculated margins ("corona radiata"), pleural retraction, size over 8 mm and upper lobe location are the morphologic signs most associated with lung carcinoma. A 3 cm solid mass with these features must be typed and staged, not followed over time.
In the report: location (lobe and segment), maximum diameter on the long and short axis, margins, relationship with the hilum, mediastinum and pleura (T), hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes (N), any other nodules, effusion, visible metastases (M). Size matters for the T stage: T1c > 2-3 cm, T2a > 3-4 cm.
Compare with the case of benign spiculated nodules: the appearance is a guide, but the diagnosis is histologic.
